name: 5th Kup

practical.title: Pattern set by the grading examiner

theory.question: Meaning of Blue Belt
theory.answer: Blue stands for the heaven toward which a growing plant reaches, becoming a tall tree, as Tae Kwon-Do training advances.

theory.question: Two Step Sparring
theory.answer: A drill for intermediate students to learn more advanced techniques. Timing and distance match three step sparring, but the attacks are more varied, so the attacker can build different combinations.

sparring: TWO STEP SPARRING (IBO MATSOKI): Attacker starts right leg back, forearm guarding block. Defence starts in parallel ready stance.
1. Attack = High punch, front kick. Defence = Left leg back, walking stance, rising block; right leg back, walking stance, X fist pressing block. Counter = Twin vertical punch.

2. Attack = Side punch, fixed stance, turning kick. Defence = Right leg back, L stance, upward palm block; left leg back, L stance, waist block. Counter = Slide forward into right L stance, right side elbow.

3. Attack = Front kick, twin vertical punch. Defence = Right leg back, walking stance, X fist pressing block; left leg back, walking stance, outer forearm wedging block. Counter = Knee kick, at the same time pull opponent's shoulders.

4. Attack = Flat fingertip thrust, side kick. Defence = Right leg back, walking stance, knifehand rising block; left leg back, L stance, inward palm block. Counter = Front kick to coccyx, twin upset punch to kidneys.

THREE STEP SEMI-FREE SPARRING (BAN JAYOO MATSOKI), Intermediate Level: Attackers start in L stance, guarding block; defenders start in parallel stance. The attacker starts with either leg back every time.

Attack = Kicking with back leg first, any kick in any order from: front kick, side kick, turning kick, reverse side kick. Defence = Any block suitable for each individual kick. Counter = Any hand attack.

otherSections.heading: Sheet note
items: Variations of the grading format are at the examiner's discretion; the sheet is for guidance only.

otherSections.heading: Yul-Gok pattern summary
items: 38 movements; starts in parallel ready stance; named for the scholar Yi I (1536-1584), nicknamed the 'Confucius of Korea'; the 38 refers to his birthplace at 38 degrees latitude.
